extracted.intended_audience: individuals, organizations, regulated parties, and their counsel who may file petitions for rulemaking or exemptions with the Federal Trade Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for submitting, docketing, supporting, and resolving petitions to the Federal Trade Commission requesting issuance, amendment, repeal, or exemption of Commission rules or interpretive rules (including industry guides). Covers what must be filed, filing mechanics, confidentiality, public notice/comment, and criteria for disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of petitions (§1.31(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule administered by the Commission pursuant to Section 18(a)(1)(B) of the FTC Act or other statutory authorities; a request to issue, amend, or repeal an interpretive rule (including an industry guide) may also be submitted by petition; a 'petition' means a written request to issue, amend, or repeal a rule or interpretive rule administered by the Commission or a petition seeking an exemption from the coverage of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what matters are petitionable: substantive rules, interpretive rules/industry guides, and exemption requests. Establishes that petitions must be written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's identity and interest (§1.31(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must include the petitioner's full name, address, telephone number, and email address (if available), along with an explanation of how the petitioner's interests would be affected by the requested action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete contact information and a clear statement of standing/interest so the petition can be docketed and the petitioner notified and contacted about the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full statement of action requested (§1.31(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must include a full statement of the action requested by the petitioner, including the text and substance of the proposed rule or amendment, or a statement identifying the rule proposed to be repealed, and citation to any existing Commission rules that would be affected by the requested action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing new or amended text, include full proposed language; when seeking repeal, identify the specific rule. Cite affected Commission rules to clarify scope and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full factual and legal basis (§1.31(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must include a full statement of the factual and legal basis on which the petitioner relies for the action requested, including all relevant facts, views, argument, and data upon which the petitioner relies, as well as information known to the petitioner that is unfavorable to the petitioner's position. The statement should identify the problem the requested action is intended to address and explain why the requested action is necessary to address the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose both supporting and unfavorable information; explicitly identify the problem and explain necessity. Provide thorough legal reasoning and fact development to permit agency evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting data standards (§1.31(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an original research report is used to support a petition, the information should be presented in a form that would be acceptable for publication in a peer reviewed scientific or technical journal. If quantitative data are used to support a petition, the presentation of the data should include a complete statistical analysis using conventional statistical methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred sources of information include professional journal articles, research reports, official government statistics, official government reports, industry data, and scientific textbooks. Original research should meet peer-review publication norms; quantitative presentations should include full statistical analyses (methods, results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing mechanics and docketing (§1.31(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition should be submitted via email to electronicfilings@ftc.gov or sent via postal mail/commercial delivery to Federal Trade Commission, Office of the Secretary, Suite CC-5610, 600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20580. If the petition meets the requirements for Commission consideration, the Secretary will assign a docket number to the petition and notify the petitioner in writing and provide an agency contact for inquiries; the petition number should be referenced in all contacts with the agency regarding the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified submission channels exactly. After docketing, use the assigned petition number in all communications. The agency will provide written notification and a contact person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment procedures (§1.31(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition contains material for which the petitioner seeks confidential treatment, the petitioner must file a request for confidential treatment that complies with §4.9(c) and provide two versions of the petition and all supporting materials (a confidential and a public version). Every page must be labeled 'Public' or 'Confidential'; confidential versions must use brackets or conspicuous markings to indicate claimed confidential material; public versions must redact material for which confidential treatment is requested. The written request must include a description of the material and the factual and legal basis for the request. Requests will be granted only if the General Counsel grants the request in accordance with law and the public interest pursuant to §4.9(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare both redacted public and marked confidential versions; include a written legal/factual justification for confidentiality. Expect the General Counsel to review and approve confidentiality consistent with §4.9(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and comment period (§1.31(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: After a petition has been docketed, the Office of the Secretary will provide public notice of the petition in the Federal Register and publish the document online for public comment for 30 days through the Federal eRulemaking portal at https://www.regulations.gov. Any person may file a statement in support of or in opposition to a petition prior to Commission action; all comments become part of the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a 30-day public comment window on regs.gov; prepare to solicit or respond to public comments. All submitted comments will be publicly accessible and included in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution standards and possible dispositions (§1.31(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant or deny a petition in whole or in part. If the Commission determines to commence a rulemaking proceeding in response to a petition, it will publish a rulemaking notice in the Federal Register and serve a copy of the notice on the petitioner. If the petition is insufficient to warrant commencement of a rulemaking proceeding, the Commission will make public its determination and notify the petitioner, who may be given the opportunity to submit additional data. Petitions that are moot, premature, repetitive, frivolous, or which plainly do not warrant consideration may be denied or dismissed without prejudice to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible outcomes include initiating rulemaking, requesting more data, public denial, or dismissal. Grounds for dismissal include mootness, prematurity, repetition, frivolousness, or plainly not warranting consideration. Petitioners may receive opportunities to supplement deficient petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to trade regulation rules, interpretive rules, and exemptions (cross-references: §§1.6, 1.9, 1.16, 1.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated procedures apply to petitions to issue, amend, or repeal trade regulation rules issued under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the FTC Act, to petitions for issuance/amendment/repeal of interpretive rules (including industry guides), and to petitions by regulated parties seeking exemptions from Commission rules. The rules revise cross-references in §§1.6, 1.9, 1.16, and 1.25 to make clear the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions concerning trade regulation rules, industry guides, and exemption requests are all to be handled under §1.31. When seeking an exemption under specific program rules (e.g., labeling, fuel posting), follow any element-specific instructions but expect §1.31 procedures to govern processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to filing rules and subject-specific parts (Part 4.2; Parts 306, 309, 323, 500)
rubrics_metrics.description: §4.2 is amended to direct that petitions for rulemaking and petitions for exemptions be filed as prescribed in §1.31. Multiple subject-specific parts (Automotive fuel ratings and posting, Labeling requirements for alternative fuels and vehicles, Made in USA Labeling Rule, and Regulations under section 4 of the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act) are amended to state that petitions for exemptions will be handled pursuant to §1.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a subject-specific rule (e.g., fuel rating posting, label size/contents) invites petitions for exemptions, petitioners must follow §1.31 filing and processing procedures in addition to any part-specific content requirements (e.g., state size and contents of label and reasons for exemption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and access policy (preamble and statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will publish petitions for rulemaking in the Federal Register and invite public comment, provide petitioners with an agency point of contact, make properly filed petitions publicly available, and notify petitioners of Commission decisions, to promote transparency and public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale: increase transparency, promote public participation, level playing field for small entities and community groups, and restore past practice of publishing petitions for inspection. Be prepared that petitions will generally be public (subject to confidentiality rules) and that public comment may follow.
